title: ACA s. 12 — Grounds for challenge (Fifth & Seventh Schedules) (ACA s. 12)

content.overview: Section 12 governs disclosure, challenge and ineligibility of arbitrators. It incorporates the Fifth Schedule for circumstances giving rise to justifiable doubts about independence or impartiality and the Seventh Schedule for specified ineligibility, subject to the statutory waiver provision.
content.glance: Section 12 governs disclosure, challenge and ineligibility of arbitrators. It incorporates the Fifth Schedule for circumstances giving rise to justifiable doubts about independence or impartiality and the Seventh Schedule for specified ineligibility, subject to the statutory waiver provision.
content.study:
Section 12 — Grounds for challenge

A person approached in connection with a possible appointment must disclose circumstances likely to give rise to justifiable doubts as to independence or impartiality, as well as specified circumstances concerning qualifications and ability to devote sufficient time where applicable under the statutory scheme.

The Fifth Schedule provides categories that may guide assessment of justifiable doubts. Section 12(3) separately recognises challenge where circumstances exist giving rise to justifiable doubts or where the arbitrator lacks agreed qualifications.

Section 12(5) renders a person whose relationship with the parties, counsel or subject matter falls within the Seventh Schedule ineligible to be appointed, notwithstanding prior agreement, subject to the statutory proviso permitting waiver after disputes have arisen by an express agreement in writing.
